scope: Hourly observations from the twelve Beijing stations of the national monitoring network, 2020-01-01 through 2026-07-20. Produced by scripts/ingest/fetch_cnemc.py and scripts/ingest/build_beijing_air.py.

files.air_quality.csv: One row per station-hour: PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, CO and O3, with station name, code and coordinates.

sources.title: National urban air quality real-time publication
sources.mirror: quotsoft.net, which archives the hourly releases as one CSV per day
sources.notes: Ground-based regulatory monitoring, not modelled. CO is published in ug/m3 here while HJ 633-2012 tabulates its sub-index in mg/m3; see beijing_aqi_co_unit.

known_limitations: THE MEANING OF THE `hour` COLUMN IS NOT DOCUMENTED BY THE SOURCE, and the corpus's ozone metrics depend on it. Values run 0-23, which reads more naturally as the hour BEGINNING at that clock time than as the hour ending there, but neither the CNEMC publication nor the quotsoft mirror states the convention and it could not be settled from the data. It matters because HJ 663-2013 defines the daily maximum 8-hour ozone mean over windows ENDING between 08:00 and 24:00, so a one-hour shift in what the label means shifts which hours each window covers. The sensitivity was measured rather than assumed, and it is small: shifting every timestamp one hour later moves Beijing's 2023 network annual mean MDA8 from 96.2024 to 96.2359 and the 2024 figure from 95.6321 to 95.6543, and leaves the corpus's canonical ozone answer — Dongsi's 42 exceedance days in summer 2023 — completely unchanged. One registered case is sensitive at its tolerance: beijing_aqi_aggregation_order reads 74.5574 as labelled and 74.5820 shifted, against a band of 0.01. NOTHING IN THE CORPUS HAS BEEN CHANGED FOR THIS, because the ambiguity is not agent-facing: every validator and every agent reads the same column the same way, so a case remains self-consistent either way. What is at stake is the PHYSICAL interpretation of the ozone windows, not the reproducibility of any answer. Resolving it needs the source's own documentation.

Coverage is 97-99 % of nominal station-hours through 2024 and falls to 81.6 % in 2025 and 77.4 % in the partial 2026, the later data having been ingested separately. The shortfall is scattered rather than one outage, which matters disproportionately for rules counting valid 8-hour windows per day: see the rejected-case record in evals/_shared/mda8.py.
2026 is partial, ending 2026-07-20. Any window that should end earlier must be pinned in the query and enforced in code.
PM2.5 above PM10 appears in 5.4 % of station-hours, an early-record instrument artefact that decays to none from 2023 on; see datasets/README.md.
The twelve stations are the benchmark set; station_metadata.csv carries two coordinate sets for them and they differ by up to 3.5 km. See station_metadata.sources.json.

HJ 663-2013 6.1.5 requires that city-scale statistics include every valid city station and that the valid station count be at least 75 % of the city's total (50 % where the total is under four). The corpus satisfies the first half by construction — every network figure averages over the stations that report, none selects a subset — and the 75 % floor was measured rather than implemented, because on this record it does not bite: only 0.48 % of PM2.5 station-hours and 4.12 % of O3 station-hours fall below 9 of 12 stations, and no day falls below 9 overall. Screening 2024 to hours with at least 9 stations leaves the exceedance count at 23 and moves the annual mean by 0.005 ug/m3, far inside every tolerance in the corpus. Implementing it would add a convention axis to every city-scale query without changing any answer, so it is deliberately not implemented. Cases reading region_cities.csv are outside this entirely: that file is CNEMC's own city-level product, where the rule was applied upstream.
